author: The Sconi
title: Aspirus Health announces retirement of North Division chief nursing officer Lori Knitt
text:
Aspirus Health has announced the retirement of Lori Knitt, RN, MS, FACHE, who served as Vice President of Patient Care for the Aspirus North Division and Chief Nursing Officer. Knitt is retiring after more than 38 years in health care as both a clinician and leader.
Knitt joined Aspirus in April 2022 as the North Division Chief Nursing Officer. She brought experience from her previous position at Advocate Aurora Health in southeast Wisconsin. During her time at Aspirus, she was part of the North Division Leadership Team and was recognized for her collaborative approach and focus on patient-centered care.
Her tenure included efforts to strengthen nursing leadership across the division and advance initiatives that improved quality, safety, and access to local care. Among her contributions were building a collaborative divisional nursing leadership team, leading enhancements to new employee orientation programs, serving as system leader of the Readmission Team, and supporting efforts to keep patients in their home communities when possible.
Knitt also worked on improving quality and safety outcomes through partnerships within Aspirus and with outside organizations. She supported Stroke and Trauma certifications across the North Division. Her teams contributed to advancements in patient experience standards that led to recognitions such as Howard Young Medical Center’s CMS 5-Star rating for patient experience.
She created the “Refuel” employee event focused on staff engagement by bringing in speakers for connection and renewal. Knitt prioritized building relationships with staff members and community partners throughout the region.
Knitt’s ties to northern Wisconsin are longstanding; her family has operated Knitt Hardware stores in St. Germain since 1973. In retirement, she plans to spend more time with family, travel, and participate in seasonal sports activities.
“Lori’s leadership, compassion, and dedication have left a lasting impact on our patients, our teams, and the communities we serve,” said Teri Theiler, President of Aspirus Health’s North Division. “We are grateful for her years of service and wish Lori and Dan continued health and happiness in this next chapter.”
Aspirus Health stated it remains committed to maintaining stability, strong leadership, and high-quality patient care during this transition period.
Aspirus Langlade Hospital is part of the Aspirus Health network serving Antigo, Wisconsin. It operates as a full-service nonprofit hospital offering services such as emergency medicine, family medicine, orthopedic surgery as well as diagnostic imaging; it also provides specialized treatments including oncology care (official website). The facility is located at 112 East Fifth Avenue in Antigo (official website).
For further information about Aspirus Health or its facilities like Aspirus Langlade Hospital visit aspirus.org.
